textPlacement.assessment: Both Everyday care and Connection & feelings rows retain a small invitation with help, rather than treating a reach or sleeve movement as an expected achievement. The full reading’s two suitable tops, gaze/reach, sleeve invitation, advance communication, pause and gentle hands are supported by 207–208 and 100. The nine-month sleeve example remains explicitly an example within infant-wide dressing, making the 6–9 placement conditional on the small participation actually available. The necessary-care sentence retains the refusal section’s adult responsibility alongside communication and gentleness; the entry does not reproduce a lifting, positioning or dressing protocol. Public references and locators identify the correct physical PDF spans.

Both Everyday care and Play & discovery rows carry their own explicit six-month-plus-readiness condition and mention choking precautions and first aid. This matches the complete 186–188 passage, rather than promoting earlier interest into permission to start solids. The full reading’s smell, texture, naming, preparation, baby pace and proportionate assistance are supported by 187 and 189–190, with purposeful hand use on 161. Its narrow attributed account does not give food sizes, menus, utensil techniques, an emergency procedure, nutrition replacement claims or independent safety assurances. The age context separates interest from readiness and does not derive feeding permission from the movement chapter. The full choking box and material contextual examples were read; the omissions do not turn this perspective into a care protocol. All reference spans and the 6–9 placement are supported.

Both Everyday care and A home that helps rows preserve steady sitting and feet reaching the floor for the low-table example, plus the baby attachment or similar for the tray-less family-table alternative. The complete Where to eat passage on 188–189 and Eating area table cell on 71 support optional snacks/meals, stability and social participation; 67 supports the accurately qualified earlier general high-chair preference. The 6–8 age is an attributed example, while actual sitting and fit remain the conditions for this 6–9 placement. The four-month assisted-sitting anecdote on 87 and photo/approximate dimensions on 92 remain distinct context and have not overridden the dedicated conditions. No specific equipment fit, purchase or positioning protocol is introduced. The public references are precise and correctly labeled as PDF pages.

Both Everyday care and Connection & feelings rows attribute the amount perspective to the authors and retain throwing food as a possible sign of being finished. The full reading supports the adult’s food/place responsibility and the baby’s amount choice from 191, with no extra mouthful or distracting into eating. Asking and helping end the meal are conditional on what is happening, consistent with 191 and the explicit if-they-seem-done language on 136. Neither the source’s possible 5–10 minute duration nor an automatic plate-removal rule is introduced. The first-year eating context supports 6–9 retrieval; the separately labeled 9–12 language reference is supplementary wording rather than a claim that a particular language skill is already due. This is a narrow description of the book’s perspective, without a nutrition assessment or new clinical claim.

Both Everyday care and Connection & feelings rows attribute the changing feeding/play/sleep pattern and explicitly identify it as a guide to noticing rather than a timetable. The complete Daily rhythm and Rituals units on 180–182 support the variable wake–feed–play–sleep example, play before a feed, growth and household/travel changes, familiar phrase/song cues, and coordinating with caregivers where possible. Optional park/breakfast/cultural ritual examples and early inclusion are supported without promising a developmental or health outcome. The 6–9 placement remains infant-wide situational guidance; no wake window, feed interval, forced sequence, sleeping setup or transport-sleep example is imported. The single public reference fully covers the selected claims.
